name_reason: Follows fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> convention (play/spell + palette_flash_with_sfx); no Ghidra address residual; accurately reflects behavior (play the status-effect SFX, then flash VGA DAC palette index 0 four times in the spell's signature RGB). Confirmed by decomp: outp(0x3C8/0x3C9) is VGA DAC, not PC speaker.
purpose: Status-class spell cast effect: play the SFX loaded by fd2_load_status_effect_sfx, then flash VGA DAC palette index 0 four times in the spell's signature colour.
logic_summary: Calls fd2_play_sfx_with_handle(data_fd2_audio_status_effect_sfx_handle_ptr, 0, 1). Then loops 4 times: set DAC write index to 0 (outp 0x3C8,0), write R/G/B for this spell from data_fd2_animation_spell_palette_flash_table at [pattern_id+0], [+0x24], [+0x48] (outp 0x3C9 x3), wait 1 BIOS tick, reset DAC index 0 to RGB(0,0,0) (outp 0x3C8,0 then three outp 0x3C9,0), wait 1 more tick. The flash table is 108 bytes = 36 entries x 3, laid out as three contiguous 36-byte planes (R at +0, G at +0x24, B at +0x48), indexed by pattern_id = spell_id 0x00..0x23.

params.name: pattern_id
params.semantics: Spell id (0x00..0x23). Used to index the 3-plane RGB palette flash table for the spell's signature flash colour. Caller fd2_spell_selection_menu_main passes spell_id directly.
params.reason: pattern_id is a stale generic name surviving from the prior misnaming as a PC-speaker beep pattern. The value is actually a spell_id (0x00..0x23): the caller passes spell_id and the plate itself notes 'pattern_id is spell_id'. Renaming to spell_id matches domain semantics. (Recorded only; applied in Stage 2.)

notes: src comment block (spellsel.c lines 498-516) is already concise, accurate, ASCII, consistent with the Ghidra plate, and correctly identifies VGA DAC (not PC speaker); kept as-is. Ghidra plate is detailed and consistent with the refined understanding; left untouched. The local loop variable beep_iter is also a residual from the old beep-pattern misnaming, but locals are out of scope for this stage (only function name + params are judged).
